Subject: Realtime stream disconnects during chat sessions

Monica —

We started seeing a pattern yesterday afternoon where a subset of our users in the triage queue are losing their interactive sessions. Symptoms: the client shows a 0-length response then client-side timeout after ~12s, and the server logs intermittently show 5xx and a few 429 spikes. This is affecting our live ops team; they have to refresh and re-open conversations which causes a poor support experience.

Attached is a small log bundle (logs_0727.txt) and a sample session id (session_sample_3345.json).

Can you confirm whether this looks like something on our side (SDK/timeouts) or if it's on Redwood's routing/runtime? We have a call scheduled Monday but wanted to surface asap.

Thanks,
Sophie King\Head of Support, Clearwell Diagnostics

Sophie — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're looking.

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether your frontend SDK has a short idle timeout/reconnect behavior enabled (client-side keepalive < 20s) and whether you apply automatic immediate retries on failures? Both patterns can surface as noisy short-lived streams and generate retry storms that cascade into 5xx/429 on our routing layer.

Action we are taking now: I've looped in Ben from Accounts and Marissa from Engineering to triage. We'll aim to have an interim mitigation within hours and follow up with a runbook.

Proposed temporary workaround for your engineers before our call: increase the SDK idle detection to 60s and disable immediate retry (exponential backoff with jitter instead). If you want, we can provide a patched JS snippet as a stop-gap.

—Monica

Quick triage update (we ran traces overnight):

- Observed a correlated spike in short-lived streaming sessions originating from a handful of Clearwell client IPs between 2027-07-27T22:00:00Z and 2027-07-28T02:00:00Z.
- Edge logs show an uptick in 429s on the region's gateway (~3x baseline) and a small increase in internal 5xx from the session aggregator layer.
- Root cause hypothesis: aggressive client retry logic + low idle TCP keepalive in the SDK causing connection tear-downs that produce a large number of ephemeral streams; the routing layer's backpressure then triggers token bucket rejections (429) and overload errors (5xx) under burst.

What we tested: applied a canary config on one serving pool that increases idle stream timeout and enables a small request coalescing window; we saw measured improvement: 60% drop in 429s for that pool and reduced tail latency for streaming handshake.

Immediate recommended steps:
1) Provide Clearwell with the SDK snippet to increase client idle timeout to >=60s and exponential backoff for retries (Monica to coordinate).
2) Roll the keepalive/canary config to two additional pools as a temporary mitigation; Ops can do this in the next 60–90 minutes.
3) Request Clearwell to disable any client-side immediate retry for 30 minutes while we roll mitigations.

I'll open INFRA-9876 with the telemetry we've captured. We should follow with a postmortem and a long-term fix to better detect retry storms from clients and apply adaptive throttling.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole\Staff SRE, Inference Runtime

Sophie/Alex — thanks for your patience. Engineering confirmed a retry-storm pattern that is amplifying short-lived streaming opens into gateway 429s. We ran a limited canary and saw significant improvement.

Short-term mitigation (please apply immediately on your side):
- Increase SDK idle detection to 60s (we attached JS/TS snippet).
- Disable immediate retry; use exponential backoff with jitter (recommended backoff: 500ms -> 1s -> 2s).

What we are doing on our side:
- Rolling canary keepalive config to two more serving pools (started, ~40 minute rollout).
- Temporarily increasing per-customer soft limits for Clearwell while we stabilize.

We will follow up with a formal incident write-up and a proposed credit for the impacted windows (HubSpot record: company CW-2026-09). Call remains on for 10:30 PT today to walk through the steps and confirm the workaround.
